messages.subject: ddply question
parts:
How come pct doesn't work in this ddply call?
 library(plyr)
b <- structure(list(SampleDate = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L,
1L, 1L, 1L), .Label = "5/8/1996", class = "factor"), TotalCount = c(1L,
2L, 1L, 1L, 4L, 3L, 1L, 10L, 3L), ForkLength = c(61L, 22L, NA,
NA, 72L, 34L, 100L, 23L, 25L), TotalSalvage = c(12L, 24L, 12L,
12L, 17L, 23L, 31L, 12L, 15L), Age = c(1L, 0L, NA, NA, 1L, 0L,
1L, 0L, 0L)), .Names = c("SampleDate", "TotalCount", "ForkLength",
"TotalSalvage", "Age"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA,
-9L))
b
ddply(b,.(SampleDate,Age),summarise,salvage=sum(TotalSalvage),pct=TotalCount/sum(TotalCount))
Error: expecting result of length one, got : 4

#Computing TotalCount inside ddply works but the pct seems wrong...
ddply(b,.(SampleDate,Age),summarise,salvage=sum(TotalSalvage),Count=sum(TotalCount),pct=Count/sum(Count))

On Tue, Sep 2, 2014 at 6:30 PM, Brandon Hurr <brando...@gmail.com> wrote:
> It's exactly what it says. You are returning 4 values.

Not that there's anything wrong with returning 4 values, AFAIK. For example,


ddply(b,
.(SampleDate,Age),
summarise,
pct=TotalCount/sum(TotalCount))

works perfectly fine. The problem is that one summary (pct) returns as
many values as there are rows in the group, and the other (salvage)
returns one value, no matter how many members are in the group. If we
fix that

ddply(b,
.(SampleDate,Age),
summarise,
salvage=rep(sum(TotalSalvage), length(TotalSalvage)),
pct=TotalCount/sum(TotalCount))

it also works, though of course we can do this more concisely with mutate:

ddply(b,.(SampleDate,Age),
mutate,
pct=TotalCount/sum(TotalCount),
salvage=sum(TotalSalvage))


>
> Perhaps you mean:
> pct=mean(TotalCount/sum(TotalCount))

Yes, perhaps.

Best,
Ista
